correctness.rationale: For arbitrary n and pool m, triangle classification is exact. At n<=b m^(2/3), noncommon-key 3-cycles, keys with at least four hits, and double witnesses have union bounds O_b(m^-1), O_b(m^-1/3), O_b(m^-2). Pair coupling costs <=n/m. Poisson splitting yields independent Gamma(3,2/m) third key hits, with local intensity 4t^2 dt du. Poisson clock de-Poissonization has vanishing m^(2/3)-scaled time error. Quantitative fixed-time TV: a=2n iid draws to K~Pois(a) alters the triple-hit count with probability at most m^-2 E|K-a| binom(max(K,a),2)=O_b(m^-1/3); independent Poisson key occupancies give binomial(m,q), Le Cam mq^2=O_b(m^-1), and |mq-4t^3/3|=O_b(m^-1/3). All claims proven analytically; exact finite checker validates structural identities, not the infinite convergence.

originality.rationale: The 2009 Yağan–Makowski exact-model paper settles only the zero-one existence threshold. Arratia–Garibaldi–Kilian give collision limits for ordinary occupancy, not two-key graph triangles; Rybarczyk–Stark establish a Poisson count result for an independent Bernoulli key model. The marked full graph-triangle birth process, unique witness principle at the critical scale and quantified O_b(m^-1/3) fixed-time approximation require nontrivial transfer and are not identified as covered by those statements or published database hits. Theoretical novelty is qualified by remaining historical-priority risk, especially later inaccessible graph-subgraph literature.
residual_risks: Other Poisson limit theorems on triangles in uniform fixed-key models may pre-exist outside the inspected papers and database results.
The 2021–2023 Dong–Hu triangular subgraph count paper was not read in full; its abstract concerns the binomial-key model and thus does not establish whole-document absence.

Classical multivariate birthday occupancy literature may have an implicit marked-third-occurrence result; novelty is claimed only for the graph-process transfer and quantitative statement, not bare occupancy limits.

value.rationale: A zero-one threshold alone does not give the probability of triangle-free status at the natural critical scale, the entire arrival timeline or the common-key label of the first triangle. This natural graph/network clustering observable has a structurally explicit Poisson point process and a uniform quantified finite-time approximation. The result is not a renaming of occupancy: it proves the negligible competing three-key cycles and within-vertex key dependence, and turns birthday statistics into graph triangles with a usable error.
